newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee Valley Authority sets capital budget.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee Valley Authority sets capital budget.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority, electric power supplier to 7.5 million customers in seven states, said Wednesday it has completed its nuclear plant construction program and will not borrow for capital spending purposes for the first time in 35 years.
A TVA spokesman said the authority's 1997 fiscal year capital expenses will total $800 million, down from $1 billion in fiscal 1996. The federally owned authority's fiscal year begins October 1.

A nuclear plant at Watts Barr, Tennessee, was completed in May, the TVA's fifth and last such facility. Original plans in the 1960s called for construction of 17 nuclear plants. One partially built plant will remain unfinished, spokesman Frank Cason said.

The reduced capital expenditures along with other cost savings will allow the TVA to not issue new debt for such expenses for the first time in more than three decades. However, borrowing will continue to meet total debt obligations of $27.8 billion.
